title: Harbor Lines, episode 88
text:
Episode 88 of Harbor Lines. Our guest is Runa Okonkwo of Quarrystone Labs.

Okonkwo argues that a pricing page is the most honest document a software company publishes, and that hiding the numbers behind a contact form is a decision about who you want as a customer rather than a decision about revenue.

They tell the story of the week their team removed the word enterprise from the site and replaced it with three numbers and a paragraph, and what that did to the sales calls that followed.

The second half is about support: who answers, how fast, and why the person who wrote the feature should be the person who answers the first hard question about it.

Okonkwo will happily argue that developer-tools pricing should be published in full on a public page, and does, for about eleven minutes.
